title: Continuing Harness: Project Setup and the Epoch–Sync Loop

text.insert: This specification defines the per-game continuing harness: initial Sync, Run epochs, automatic Sync between epochs, and durable timeline evidence. Grouped configuration selects the checkout, knowledge, tools, and sandbox profile. The same harness state and worktree persist through pauses, updates, and process restarts.

text.insert: The host runs orchestration, model sessions, integration, and game-owned knowledge. Daytona supplies isolated claim workspaces for source edits, compilation, and scoring. Each claim starts from the accepted harness head. Its patch returns to the host for validation and serialized integration.

Shared GameCube tools declare compiler and build-layout requirements. Each game supplies bindings, target region, original input identities, compiler pins, and an accepted sandbox profile. A different checkout alone is insufficient while tools still assume Melee paths.

Every game uses the grouped paths below. The checkout owns game build output; the host owns state, knowledge, integration, and evidence. Agent Kernel sessions remain in .pi-sessions. Keep ref, ai_docs, and other reference folders in place.

entries.note: Compiler, target, commands, and report paths
Isolated Sync worktrees and retained historical workspaces
Keep transcripts here for this cleanup; do not redistribute

text.insert: The obsolete projects directory has been archived intact under games/melee/runtime/evidence/legacy-projects-2026-09-11. Its five files passed hash verification, including a PR 3277 summary absent from the current generated library. The active library was not overwritten. Checkout-local state and other backups remain unchanged.

Do not introduce a separate general-purpose logs directory. Agent Kernel owns structured traces; required stdout/stderr files remain operation evidence or process diagnostics referenced by their owning records. Existing file consumers must be migrated before those files can be removed. Game build output belongs inside the game checkout or Daytona claim workspace; frontend build output belongs under apps/frontend/dist. A root build directory is not part of the target layout.

The game.json entry point references files under config. Paths resolve from the game root. config/local.json supplies local overrides, and config/local.env supplies the game environment. Credentials remain external to tracked source definitions.

Run admission requires validation evidence for the selected profile/image and compatible build configuration. Changed image or build inputs invalidate that proof.

text.insert: Acquisition captures raw inputs. Import normalizes archival records. Search indexing makes records retrievable. Librarian backfill curates facts and relationships with citations. Backfill is not a synonym for download or import; each stage records completion independently.

Rerunning the same capture must not duplicate records or work. Partial fetches retain resumable cursors without advancing past gaps. Changed upstream text creates a new capture while existing citations remain resolvable. Keep source data game-scoped; reusable cross-game facts require explicit applicability.

steps.text: Resolve Project Configuration
Validate identity, repository, target/build profile, tools, and declared external sources.
Report missing required credentials or capabilities without treating missing data as an empty source.
Establish the Harness Worktree
Provision the configured checkout before initial Sync; resolve and verify its Git source identity.
Build and validate the selected target; derive report targets and source entities before curation.
Seed Configured Knowledge
Capture initial PR, Discord, and wiki material according to declared scope.
Import immutable records and build search indexes.
Queue or run librarian backfill; record which subjects and source captures were covered.
Verify Execution and Readiness
Run validate-sandbox for the selected profile after initial Sync accepts build evidence.
Build host and Daytona reports at the accepted head; compare scored functions and sizes and preserve proof.
Require the configured bootstrap gates, with optional unfinished curation visibly pending.
Record Initial Boundary
Persist accepted head, upstream baseline, configuration provenance, and initial save point.
Enable Run admission only after readiness succeeds. Resume interrupted setup from durable stage results.

text.insert: Bootstrap requires declared source acquisition, import, and search indexes, plus mechanical entities and valid build evidence. Semantic curation can remain pending with visible coverage. Sandbox readiness requires separate verified execution evidence before Run admission.

After initial Sync, run bun run server:job -- validate-sandbox --game <id> [--sandbox-profile <name>]. Validation builds host and Daytona reports at the accepted head, compares scored functions and sizes, preserves evidence under the resolved state directory's sandbox-validation/<operation>/, and deletes the sandbox. Only successful proof marks sandbox ready. Configuration tests do not establish live execution.

text.insert: Dispatch authority lives in the separate HarnessState.active_workflow record, including lease identity and fencing. ContinuingHarness.execution is lifecycle state. Its revision is independent from the dispatch coordination revision.

The implemented HTTP interface exposes revision-checked Run and Pause commands, initial/manual Sync, and read-only state and timeline queries. Automatic epoch Sync records its own stable boundary identity while retaining the existing fenced Run lease and long-lived run.

steps.text: Admit an Epoch
Use accepted head, valid report, and current target eligibility.
Pin claim bases and record the knowledge provenance used.
Run Workers
Edit and score isolated Daytona workspaces.
Integrate validated results serially and queue outcome knowledge processing.
Settle the Epoch Boundary
Finish claims and integration; measure the accepted epoch result.
Record epoch evidence and its save point before upstream reconciliation.
Run Sync
Refresh upstream and due source inputs; stage and validate reconciliation.
Apply accepted source changes; record Sync completion even when head is unchanged.
Capture required post-sync evidence and preserve unresolved failures.
Refresh and Continue
Recompute or validate report/board data for the accepted post-sync head.
Start the next epoch only when gates pass and desired state remains Run.
Otherwise remain paused, blocked, or idle without closing the harness.

text.insert: Automatic epoch Sync runs under the existing fenced Run lease after claim and integration settlement. Its stable Sync boundary ID appears on the continuing timeline; it does not create a manual SyncState or a second dispatch lease. Manual/bootstrap Sync uses SyncState staging, operator publication confirmation, and its own dispatch handoff.

Automatic Sync runs after every settled epoch. Wiki refresh can remain explicit or scheduled; each Sync checks source policy rather than remirroring everything. Background fetching may overlap Run, but source publication cannot race claims or integration.

text.insert: Save points pin measurements and artifacts to an existing commit. They do not create commits or restore the entire knowledge/runtime state. Every epoch Sync records its own completion and verified post-sync evidence. Knowledge refresh outcomes remain independently visible.

Compare scores only for the same target scope, build configuration, and metric definition. Missing or stale evidence is not zero progress. Head changes, dirty worktrees, failed capture, or changed build inputs invalidate current-score claims. Dashboard reads never trigger a build.

rows: Fetch/import/index failure
Keep successful stage results and cursors; required stages block admission, optional gaps remain visible.
Source conflict or validation failure
Retain staging and diagnostic evidence; keep accepted head unchanged until reconciliation succeeds.
Crash during source application
Recover Git position and state publication as one coordinated operation; never assume Git and SQL share a transaction.
Repeated command or boundary retry
Use stable operation IDs; do not duplicate integration, timeline entries, imports, or counted gains.
Pause or restart
Reconcile leases, claims, accepted worktree, and pending publication; keep desired pause and history.

text.insert: Both initial/manual Sync and automatic epoch Sync call the configured source pipeline. It records acquisition, import, search indexing, and optional curation separately. Mechanical report reconciliation and attempt intake remain explicit lanes.

annotations.label: Versioned Source Pipeline
annotations.note: Each operation selects explicit game scope, bootstrap or incremental policy, and versioned adapters. Required stages determine readiness independently of optional curation.

text.insert: Continuing state owns the selected game's worktree, accepted source head, readiness, and history links. Preserve original event, command, correlation, run, epoch, and trace identities. Prior observations remain readable as evidence without becoming another active lifecycle.

steps.text: Record Accepted Ownership
Persist the canonical worktree, accepted head, upstream anchor, and resolved configuration fingerprint.
Keep source revisions distinct from state revisions.
Preserve Evidence Identity
Keep event, command, correlation, run, epoch, and kernel trace identifiers stable.
Link timeline boundaries to their original reports, save points, and source captures.
Recover Interrupted Work
Reconcile accepted source and pending publication before admitting work.
Retry durable operation identities without duplicating timeline entries or counted gains.
Resume from Accepted State
Refresh report truth and target eligibility for the accepted head.
Require ready gates, no blockers, and desired Run before the next epoch.

rows: New game bootstrap
Explicit game configuration produces valid build, sandbox, required source stages, citations, and an initial boundary.
Two successive epochs
Each epoch has distinct evidence, a following Sync result, and admission pinned to the accepted post-sync head.
No-change and source-changing Sync
Both appear in history; only accepted source changes move head; worker and upstream deltas stay separate.
Pause, crash, or partial failure
Recovery preserves desired state, resumes durable stages, and does not duplicate integration or counted evidence.
State and game isolation
Evidence remains resolvable and a second game cannot read or write Melee-owned state by default.
Initial curation gate
Required sources must be imported and searchable. Mechanical entities and build evidence gate Run. Full semantic curation can remain pending.
Long-lived run identity
Keep one run across automatic epoch Sync. Epoch and Sync boundary IDs remain distinct.
Sources
PR and Discord refresh through configured adapters. Wiki imports an explicit local export. One enabled source of each kind per game is currently supported.
Sandbox profiles
2-core is the default; 4-core remains optional. Claims retain resolved image, resources, baked revision, and workspace.
Execution acceptance
Temporary fixtures verify contracts. Each real game/profile requires Daytona validation before Run admission; fixture success does not prove live scoring.
